description: Unique microVM identifier. Used as the cgroup leaf name and chroot subdirectory. Must be unique per host since the chroot path collides on duplicates.
Non-privileged uid the Firecracker process runs as. Must have read+write access to /dev/kvm (typically via the kvm group). Production: per-microVM unique uid for additional isolation.
Non-privileged gid. Common pattern: gid in the kvm group for /dev/kvm access.
Cgroup hierarchy version. v2 recommended for production (snapshot restore is significantly slower under v1 — see snapshots leaf).

Cgroup setting written by jailer when creating the leaf cgroup. Examples: cpuset.cpus=0, cpu.shares=512 (v1), cpu.max='100000 100000' (v2 — 100ms quota per 100ms period), memory.max=536870912 (v2 — 512 MiB cap).

Relative parent cgroup path. Lets orchestrators nest microVM cgroups (e.g., 'fleet/tenant_A'). On v2 + no --cgroup, jailer MOVES the process to this existing cgroup — exits with error if it has subtree-controllers enabled.
Base directory for chroot trees. Final chroot path: <base>/<exec_file_name>/<id>/root. Set to a fast disk (NVMe) for snapshot-heavy workloads.
Path to a network namespace handle (e.g., /var/run/netns/myvm or /proc/<pid>/ns/net). Jailer setns()s into it before exec. If omitted, Firecracker shares the host's netns — much weaker isolation.
Max file size (bytes) the Firecracker process can create. Use to bound runaway snapshot-mem files. Applied via setrlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE).

Max FD count for the Firecracker process. setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE). 2048 is sufficient for moderate device counts; raise for vsock-heavy or VirtIO-MMIO-dense guests (Firecracker uses 20+ FDs by baseline).
setsid() + redirect stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null. Useful when launching from a non-systemd orchestrator. Do NOT combine with structured logging that expects the original tty.
Spawn Firecracker into a new PID namespace via clone(CLONE_NEWPID). Firecracker appears as PID 1 inside the namespace; host-side PID is recorded in <chroot_dir>/<exec_file_name>.pid.
